cards.front: sound
cards.back: A form of energy made by vibrations. It travels as waves.
cards.say: sound. A form of energy made by vibrations. It travels as waves.

cards.front: vibration
cards.back: A quick movement backwards and forwards.
cards.say: vibration. A quick movement backwards and forwards.

cards.front: What does sound need to travel through?
cards.back: A material such as a solid, liquid or gas. Sound cannot travel through empty space.
cards.say: What does sound need to travel through? A material such as a solid, liquid or gas. Sound cannot travel through empty space.

cards.front: Does sound travel fastest in solids, liquids or gases?
cards.back: Solids. It is slowest in gases, such as air.
cards.say: Does sound travel fastest in solids, liquids or gases? Solids. It is slowest in gases, such as air.

cards.front: pitch
cards.back: How high or low a sound is.
cards.say: pitch. How high or low a sound is.

cards.front: How can you make a sound with a higher pitch?
cards.back: Make the vibrations faster. A shorter, tighter or thinner string gives a higher pitch.
cards.say: How can you make a sound with a higher pitch? Make the vibrations faster. A shorter, tighter or thinner string gives a higher pitch.

cards.front: frequency
cards.back: The number of vibrations in each second. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch.
cards.say: frequency. The number of vibrations in each second. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch.

cards.front: hertz
cards.back: The unit of frequency. One hertz is one vibration each second.
cards.say: hertz. The unit of frequency. One hertz is one vibration each second.

cards.front: loudness
cards.back: How loud a sound is. It is measured in decibels.
cards.say: loudness. How loud a sound is. It is measured in decibels.

cards.front: How can you make a sound louder?
cards.back: Make bigger vibrations, for example by hitting a drum harder.
cards.say: How can you make a sound louder? Make bigger vibrations, for example by hitting a drum harder.

cards.front: amplitude
cards.back: The size of a vibration. A bigger amplitude gives a louder sound.
cards.say: amplitude. The size of a vibration. A bigger amplitude gives a louder sound.

cards.front: Which has a higher pitch: a short thin guitar string or a long thick one?
cards.back: The short thin one.
cards.say: Which has a higher pitch: a short thin guitar string or a long thick one? The short thin one.

cards.front: Which has a lower pitch: a long pipe or a short pipe?
cards.back: The long pipe.
cards.say: Which has a lower pitch: a long pipe or a short pipe? The long pipe.

cards.front: What happens to the pitch if you tighten a guitar string?
cards.back: It gets higher.
cards.say: What happens to the pitch if you tighten a guitar string? It gets higher.

cards.front: echo
cards.back: A sound that bounces off a hard surface and is heard again.
cards.say: echo. A sound that bounces off a hard surface and is heard again.

cards.front: Which materials absorb sound well?
cards.back: Soft materials such as carpet, curtains and foam.
cards.say: Which materials absorb sound well? Soft materials such as carpet, curtains and foam.

cards.front: About how fast does sound travel in air?
cards.back: About 340 metres each second.
cards.say: About how fast does sound travel in air? About three hundred and forty metres each second.

cards.front: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
cards.back: Light travels much faster than sound.
cards.say: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder? Light travels much faster than sound.

cards.front: eardrum
cards.back: A thin skin inside the ear. Sound makes it vibrate.
cards.say: eardrum. A thin skin inside the ear. Sound makes it vibrate.

cards.front: How do we hear a sound?
cards.back: Sound waves make the eardrum vibrate. Tiny bones pass the vibrations on and nerves send signals to the brain.
cards.say: How do we hear a sound? Sound waves make the eardrum vibrate. Tiny bones pass the vibrations on and nerves send signals to the brain.

cards.front: Why do some workers wear ear defenders?
cards.back: Very loud sounds can damage hearing. Ear defenders absorb some of the sound.
cards.say: Why do some workers wear ear defenders? Very loud sounds can damage hearing. Ear defenders absorb some of the sound.
